note: The only psoriasis-specific animal evidence any regulator saw was a human-skin xenograft dosed with a different anti-p19 antibody; tildrakizumab and mirikizumab both cleared phase 3 on PASI, LY2525623 was stopped after eight patients, and mirikizumab's psoriasis filing was withdrawn for business reasons.
label: Psoriasis (IL-23 p19)

engagement.model: Human psoriasis skin xenograft on AGR129 mice (anti-p19 clone 7G10)
engagement.note: Readouts were acanthosis and CD3+ T cells; IL-17 and IFN-gamma transcripts did not move with anti-IL-23 in the graft, IL-22 only trended down.
engagement.short: Xenograft readout was histology, not cytokines
engagement.quote: Injection of a mAb specifically neutralizing human IL-23 showed IL-23-dependent inhibition of psoriasis development comparable to the use of anti-TNF blockers in a clinically relevant xenotransplant mouse model of psoriasis.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read on PMC (PMC3776381); the cytokine detail is from the results text, the quote is the abstract.
engagement.judgement: Opens the strip: the one psoriasis-specific in-vivo system a member's regulator relied on (EPAR: 'the most relevant in vivo efficacy data'). It was dosed with Schering-Plough's mouse anti-human IL-23 clone 7G10 at 60 mg/kg, not a member, so product_in_model is false.

engagement.model: Human psoriasis skin xenograft on AGR129 mice (anti-p19 clone 7G10)
engagement.note: Tildrakizumab phase 1 biopsies showed the histological improvement the xenograft measured; the sponsor found no target-engagement biomarker (total IL-23 undetectable, EPAR).
engagement.short: Lesional histology improved as in xenograft
engagement.quote: Tildrakizumab demonstrated important clinical improvement in moderate-to-severe psoriasis patients as demonstrated by improvements in PASI scores and histological samples.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (Nature paywalled); the biopsy detail was not read. EPAR 2018: 'No useful biomarkers of target engagement (total IL-23), dose response or activity (IL-22, calprotectin) were identified.'
engagement.reason: Histology moved; no direct engagement marker
engagement.judgement: Scored on the readout the model actually used (acanthosis, T-cell infiltrate), which is downstream of the target; the model's own cytokine readouts were null in the mouse and the sponsor found no engagement biomarker in people, so readout_tier is downstream and confidence medium. Dated to the Nature epub (2015-03-09); the phase 1 (P05382) has no public registry results record I could find.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of lesional histology (epidermal thickness, infiltrate)

engagement.confidence_note: Proxy first-use year: the IND 125444 pharmacology reviews (Reference ID 3809521) summarise studies filed before the psoriasis first-in-human NCT01947933 (first posted 2013-09-23). Model data first public in Steere 2023 JPET (doi 10.1124/jpet.122.001512, epub 2023-09-15) and this review.
engagement.model: Acute systemic human IL-23 neutralisation in mice dosed with mirikizumab (ex-vivo splenocyte IL-17)
engagement.note: Mice primed i.p. with human IL-23 plus IL-2; mirikizumab blocked the ex-vivo anti-CD3 IL-17 response of splenocytes. No member trial measured serum or ex-vivo IL-17.
engagement.quote: In an acute systemic in vivo neutralization assay in mice, LY3074828 inhibited human IL-23-induced IL-17 production.
engagement.judgement: Mirikizumab does not bind rodent IL-23, so this human-cytokine priming assay is its only systemic in-vivo engagement readout. Mirikizumab's psoriasis phase 1 (NCT01947933) reported PK and AEs only and OASIS-1/2 list no cytokine outcome, so nobody compared it with patients.
engagement.reason: No member trial measured IL-17 ex vivo

engagement.confidence_note: Proxy first-use year 2013 (pre-IND study, Report 192, reviewed under IND 125444; psoriasis FIH NCT01947933 first posted 2013-09-23). Quote is the reviewer's study-report summary; model data first public in Steere 2023 JPET (epub 2023-09-15).
engagement.model: Acute local intradermal human IL-23 mouse skin assay dosed with mirikizumab (IL-17A/IL-17F/keratin-16 mRNA, epidermal thickening)
engagement.note: Two days of intradermal human IL-23 induced IL-17A, IL-17F and keratin-16 mRNA with epidermal thickening; one s.c. mirikizumab dose abrogated all three, isotype did not.
engagement.quote: Intradermal injection of human IL-23 induced mRNA expression of IL-17A and IL-17F, and this was abrogated by the treatment with LY3074828 but not isotype control antibody.
engagement.judgement: A different system from the systemic assay: skin-local IL-23 with a psoriasis-like readout (keratin-16, epidermal thickening) rather than splenocyte priming, so it gets its own track. Product dosed, so product_in_model true.

engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of lesional IL-23-pathway transcript change; no shared quantity
engagement.confidence_note: Nature paywalled: quote is the Figure 6 caption ('Tildrakizumab inhibits IL-23-associated psoriatic skin gene expression'); which genes were on the panel (IL-17A, IL-17F, K16 are the model's) could not be read. Patient side is a sibling member (tildrakizumab); mirikizumab's own psoriasis trials report no skin PD. Year is 2023 because the model data were not public before Steere 2023 JPET (epub 2023-09-15); the model predates the 2013 FIH, so not a retrodiction. Phase 1 registry record not retrieved.
engagement.model: Acute local intradermal human IL-23 mouse skin assay dosed with mirikizumab (IL-17A/IL-17F/keratin-16 mRNA, epidermal thickening)
engagement.note: Kopp 2015: lesional NanoString panel of IL-23-associated genes, all raised in lesional skin, fell after three tildrakizumab doses. Paired here once Lilly's model was public (2023).
engagement.short: Lesional IL-23-pathway genes fell in patients
engagement.quote: All genes were detectably increased in lesional skin compared with non-lesional skin, and were significantly decreased by at least one tildrakizumab dose using a P < 0.05 criteria in the Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank test.
engagement.judgement: Model readout (IL-23-driven IL-17A/IL-17F/K16 transcripts in skin) and patient readout (IL-23-associated lesional gene expression) are the same downstream tier and moved the same way; direction only, and on a sibling member, so a paired comparison at low confidence.
engagement.reason: Lesional IL-23-pathway transcripts fell as modelled

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (only cross-reactive species)
dose.note: Tildrakizumab and mirikizumab bind human and cynomolgus but not mouse IL-23p19, so cynomolgus carried all PK/TK and toxicology; the class was in phase 2 by 2009.
dose.short: Cynomolgus is the only tox species
dose.quote: Thus, cynomolgus monkeys were selected as the relevant species for toxicology testing.
dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: LY2525623 was in phase 2 by December 2009 (NCT01018810 first posted 2009-11-25), so the class's cynomolgus toxicology predates that; the source is the 2018 EPAR (EMA/CHMP/664213/2018).
dose.judgement: No FDA tildrakizumab review is online (the MultidisciplineR link 404s; only the label is in the bundle), so the US filing is read through the label's monkey data and the EMA report. Mirikizumab's cynomolgus toxicology is in the FDA Omvoh review (2023), same system.

dose.note: CHMP: NOAEL 140 mg/kg (3-month) and 100 mg/kg (9-month) gave >100-200x the exposure at 200 mg q12w; patients took 100 and 200 mg with no dose-limiting toxicity.
dose.short: Cyno NOAEL margin held in patients
dose.quote: The exposure achieved in cynomolgus monkeys at the NOAEL provides a large margin to the exposure at the proposed clinical dose.
dose.reason: Tolerability margin held; no efficacy exposure target
dose.judgement: Decision 16: a stated tolerability margin that held is same with margin_stated. No model gave an efficacy exposure target: the xenograft used 60 mg/kg of a different antibody, which the EPAR itself calls 'quite high' against 200 mg, so the dose cell carries only the toxic end of the window. Mirikizumab's cynomolgus NOAEL (100 mg/kg, 6-month SC; FDA Omvoh review 2023) and its psoriasis dosing at 250 mg q4w with class-consistent safety (OASIS-1/2) agree and are not entered separately. registry_date is reSURFACE 1 results posting.
dose.magnitude_basis: NOAEL exposure margin (>100x at 200 mg q12w) against clinical tolerability

efficacy.model: Human psoriasis skin xenograft on AGR129 mice (anti-p19 clone 7G10)
efficacy.note: Anti-human IL-23 at 60 mg/kg blocked acanthosis and papillomatosis of grafted pre-psoriatic skin at 5 weeks, matching infliximab; the class prediction before any member was dosed.
efficacy.short: Xenograft: anti-IL-23 blocks psoriasis like anti-TNF
efficacy.quote: Injection of a mAb specifically neutralizing human IL-23 showed IL-23-dependent inhibition of psoriasis development comparable to the use of anti-TNF blockers in a clinically relevant xenotransplant mouse model of psoriasis.
efficacy.judgement: Prediction level is class: the grafts come from patients but the model was never used to choose who is treated. Filed with the EMA as the publication rather than a study report (EPAR p.21: 'provided in the form of a peer reviewed publication'); the FDA tildrakizumab review is not online, so model_filed rests on the EMA record.

efficacy.model: Human psoriasis skin xenograft on AGR129 mice (anti-p19 clone 7G10)
efficacy.note: Phase 1 proof of concept: every subject at 3 and 10 mg/kg reached PASI 75 by day 196; phase 2b PASI 75 at week 16 was 64-74% vs 4% (Papp 2015).
efficacy.short: Tildrakizumab PASI 75 in all high-dose subjects
efficacy.quote: A 75% reduction in the psoriasis area and severity index (PASI) score (PASI75) was achieved by all subjects in parts 1 and 3 (pooled) in the 3 and 10 mg kg(-1) groups by day 196.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Kopp 2015 (paywalled); Papp 2015 phase 2b read at abstract level.
efficacy.judgement: The phase 1 was designed 'to provide clinical proof that specific targeting of IL-23p19 results in symptomatic improvement', so endpoint_role is poc_gate; the phase 2b primary (PASI 75 at week 16, NCT01225731, results posted 2015-03-30) confirms it three weeks after the Nature epub. Paired by me: neither paper cites the xenograft as a prediction.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PASI response direction; the model reports acanthosis, not a PASI-like scale

patient_trials.quote: Tildrakizumab had treatment effects that were superior to placebo, maintained for 52 weeks of treatment, and persisted for 20 weeks after cessation.

efficacy.model: Human psoriasis skin xenograft on AGR129 mice (anti-p19 clone 7G10)
efficacy.note: CHMP took the xenograft as the proof of concept for IL-23 blockade and approved on reSURFACE 1/2: PASI 75 at week 12 62-66% vs 6% placebo, superior to etanercept.
efficacy.short: Regulator: xenograft was the proof of concept
efficacy.quote: In vivo studies in models of inflammatory bowel disease or psoriasis with IL-23p19 neutralising antibodies demonstrate pharmacologic activity and provide a proof-of-concept for the blockade of IL-23 in psoriasis.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens only: same status, a phase 3 confirmation on the primary endpoint and a regulator calling the model the proof of concept. comparison_stated is false because the nonclinical and clinical conclusions sit in different sections of the report and no sentence sets them against each other. The EPAR also notes the model's dose (60 mg/kg) was 'quite high' against 200 mg, which is why magnitude stays direction_only.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PASI 75 response direction vs placebo and etanercept

patient_trials.quote: At week 12, 192 patients (62%) in the 200 mg group and 197 patients (64%) in the 100 mg group achieved PASI 75, compared with 9 patients (6%) in the placebo group

In two phase 3 trials, tildrakizumab 200 mg and 100 mg were efficacious compared with placebo and etanercept and were well tolerated in the treatment of patients with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis.

efficacy.model: Mouse colitis with surrogate anti-mouse p19 (SCH 900598 for tildrakizumab; LSN2479016 for mirikizumab)
efficacy.note: Each sponsor's only in-vivo pharmacology with its own programme's antibody was mouse IBD with a surrogate; CHMP called it supportive, nobody compared it with PASI.
efficacy.quote: Although the disease indication differs than that in the current MAA these studies could be considered to be supportive in suggesting that the inhibition of IL-23 in inflammatory diseases can have significant effects on the pathology seen.
efficacy.confidence_note: Model year unknown; the surrogate studies are sponsor reports summarised in the EPAR and in the FDA Omvoh review (2023, 'two murine models of inflammatory bowel disease'), not published.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track because it is a different system with a different prediction (IL-23 blockade reduces gut inflammation) from the xenograft. Kept untested rather than same: transferring a colitis result to a PASI endpoint is not a comparison anyone made, and the surrogate SCH 900598 is 10-20x weaker than tildrakizumab (KD 3.5-6.7 nM vs 297 pM).

efficacy.model: Human psoriasis skin xenograft on AGR129 mice (anti-p19 clone 7G10)
efficacy.note: Second member: mirikizumab phase 2 met PASI 90 at week 16 (67% at 300 mg vs 0%); OASIS-1/2 phase 3 co-primaries met; Lilly then withdrew the psoriasis filing for business reasons.
efficacy.short: Mirikizumab met PASI 90; filing withdrawn for business
efficacy.quote: At week 16, 67% of patients treated with mirikizumab 300 mg at 8-week intervals achieved PASI 90.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Reich 2019, Blauvelt 2022 and Papp 2023.
efficacy.reason: Two members matched; LY2525623 never tested
efficacy.judgement: LY2525623 (NCT01018810) is the third member: its phase 2 was terminated after 8 patients 'for several reasons, including complexities in development of LY2525623, but not because of safety concerns' (registry; results posted 2011-06-30 with no outcome analysed), so it neither confirms nor contradicts the model and is not scored. Mirikizumab's withdrawal from psoriasis is not an efficacy failure: OASIS-2 states the sponsor 'is not pursuing licensing of mirikizumab in this patient population because of a reprioritised development strategy'. Mirikizumab's own filed in-vivo pharmacology was mouse IBD with surrogate LSN2479016 (FDA Omvoh review 2023), not a psoriasis model. registry_date is the phase 2 (NCT02899988) results posting.

patient_trials.quote: All primary and key secondary endpoints were met.
This trial showed superiority of mirikizumab at a dose of 250 mg over placebo in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, with a safety profile consistent with that of the IL-23 class.

efficacy.confidence_note: Open access (PMC8409790), full text read; online 2021-08-30. Run by a competitor (AbbVie) after tildrakizumab's phase 3 results, so the track opens as a retrodiction system.
efficacy.model: Human IL-23-induced ear-swelling mouse model, four IL-23 antibodies head-to-head incl. tildrakizumab (AbbVie 2021)
efficacy.note: Clinical-grade tildrakizumab, guselkumab, risankizumab and ustekinumab dosed in the ear model; tildrakizumab inhibited swelling and IL-17A/IL-22/S100A7a/DEFB4 expression least among the p19 antibodies.
efficacy.short: Tildrakizumab weakest p19 antibody in ear model
efficacy.quote: In a human IL-23-induced ear-swelling mouse model, risankizumab and guselkumab were more effective than ustekinumab and tildrakizumab at reducing IL-17, IL-22, and keratinocyte gene expression.
efficacy.judgement: A separate system from Lilly's intradermal PD assay: ear swelling plus a different gene panel, a comparative-potency prediction rather than product neutralisation, and run by another sponsor.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: rank order of in-vivo inhibition vs cross-trial PASI 90 among p19 antibodies
efficacy.confidence_note: Retrodiction: reSURFACE 1/2 (2017) and the guselkumab/risankizumab trials were known before the model was run. The patient comparison is cross-trial, not head-to-head, and the authors state whether the potency gap 'translates to their performance in patients is not known'.
efficacy.model: Human IL-23-induced ear-swelling mouse model, four IL-23 antibodies head-to-head incl. tildrakizumab (AbbVie 2021)
efficacy.note: Same paper sets the model rank beside clinical PASI 90 (52-59% tildrakizumab vs 76-81% guselkumab/risankizumab) and tildrakizumab's flat 100 vs 200 mg response; authors call the translation unknown.
efficacy.short: Model rank order matches cross-trial PASI 90
efficacy.quote: In this context, it is noteworthy that tildrakizumab’s clinical efficacy at a 2-fold higher dose did not increase significantly (PASI 90 of 52–59% at 100 mg and 59% at 200 mg dose).
efficacy.judgement: The paper itself juxtaposes model rank and PASI 90 (Table 1, Discussion), so comparison_stated true; the model reproduced the known rank order in direction, which the v3 rule scores retro, never same. Scored on the member only; guselkumab and risankizumab are comparators, not members.

patient_trials.quote: At week 12, 192 patients (62%) in the 200 mg group and 197 patients (64%) in the 100 mg group achieved PASI 75, compared with 9 patients (6%) in the placebo group

In two phase 3 trials, tildrakizumab 200 mg and 100 mg were efficacious compared with placebo and etanercept and were well tolerated in the treatment of patients with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; online 2006-12-21, print Feb 2007. Functional loss of function: Sarin 2011 PNAS doi 10.1073/pnas.1017854108 (epub 2011-05-23). Same model_id as the Crohn's disease tile for this mechanism.
efficacy.note: IL23R missense SNPs (R381Q, L310P) mark a psoriasis haplotype (OR 1.44) in 1,446 cases; R381Q carriers' T cells later shown to make less IL-23-dependent IL-17/IL-22 (Sarin 2011).
efficacy.short: IL23R loss-of-function allele protects from psoriasis
efficacy.quote: These data, and the previous observation that administration of an antibody specific for the IL-12p40 subunit to patients with psoriasis is highly efficacious, suggest that these genes play a fundamental role in psoriasis pathogenesis.
efficacy.judgement: The human loss-of-function genotype is an in-scope model_kind and is the class rationale Tonel 2010 cites; its prediction is that blocking IL-23 signalling treats psoriasis. No drug is dosed, so product_in_model false.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of IL-23 loss-of-function protection vs PASI 75 response
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Nature paywalled); online 2015-03-09. Paired by the drafter: no source puts IL23R R381Q beside a member trial. Registry date is the phase 2b P05495 results posting (NCT01225731, 2015-03-30), as in the draft. The one patient-level genetic test of a member (Butron-Bris 2024, 180-SNP panel, n=90) does not report IL23R.
efficacy.note: Tildrakizumab phase 1 proof-of-concept: PASI 75 in all 3 and 10 mg/kg subjects by day 196; the protective-allele direction held in dosed patients.
efficacy.short: Anti-p19 PASI response matches protective allele
efficacy.quote: Tildrakizumab demonstrated important clinical improvement in moderate-to-severe psoriasis patients as demonstrated by improvements in PASI scores and histological samples.
efficacy.judgement: Direction only: a protective allele cannot give an effect size for a PASI response, so magnitude is direction_only and the entry is a paired class-level comparison, as the Crohn's tile scored this track with Feagan 2017.

patient_trials.quote: Tildrakizumab had treatment effects that were superior to placebo, maintained for 52 weeks of treatment, and persisted for 20 weeks after cessation.

safety.note: Cynomolgus carried all toxicology for every member; the human antibodies cannot be dosed in mice, so infection and gut harms were tested with surrogates instead.
safety.short: Cyno tox is the only safety species
safety.quote: The toxicity of tildrakizumab has been adequately characterised in cynomolgus monkeys which were deemed to be the only active species for relevant pharmacological activity.
safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy (class in phase 2 by December 2009, NCT01018810); source is the 2018 EPAR.
safety.judgement: Same system as the dose track. The pre/postnatal study's neonatal deaths at 59x the MRHD ('clinical significance unknown', FDA label 8.1) is a possible harm the species raised that cannot be checked in patients, so it is not scored either way.

safety.note: Cyno predicted no systemic harm and injection-site inflammation; phase 3 serious AEs were similar and low in all arms and label injection-site reactions were 3% vs 2%.
safety.short: Clean cyno profile held in patients
safety.quote: In the repeat dose toxicity studies tildrakizumab was very well tolerated and the main findings were inflammatory infiltrates at the injection site following SC administration of the mAb.
safety.reason: Clean cyno profile held in patients
safety.judgement: Comparison sits inside one benefit-risk assessment (nonclinical and clinical sections of the EPAR), so comparison_stated is true; the patient figures are Reich 2017 ('Serious adverse events were similar and low in all groups in both trials') and the FDA label (injection site reactions 3% vs 2%, serious infections <=0.3% both arms). OASIS-2's 4 MACE vs 0 on mirikizumab (Papp 2023) is a single-trial imbalance the paper calls class-consistent and no label carries; flagged unresolved, not scored as a contradiction. registry_date is reSURFACE 1 results posting.

safety.model: Mouse intracellular-infection challenge with surrogate anti-p19 (BCG, Salmonella, Listeria)
safety.note: Surrogate-dosed mice predicted no worse infection risk than anti-p40; label: serious infections <=0.3% in both arms, upper respiratory infections 14% vs 12%.
safety.short: Mouse infection models: no excess risk, held
safety.quote: The rates of serious infections for the ILUMYA group and the placebo group were ≤0.3%.
safety.confidence_note: Placebo-controlled window is 12-16 weeks; the EPAR itself says 'impairment in host defence towards special pathogens cannot be fully excluded with the non-clinical data', so the agreement is for the trial window only.
safety.reason: No excess infection, as mice predicted
safety.judgement: Separate track: a different system with a different prediction (host defence) from the toxicology track. The model prediction is the EPAR sentence 'the data suggest that IL-23-specific blockade would not be expected to incur any worse infection risk profile in humans than the existing anti-IL-12/23p40 therapy'; paired by me with the label, so comparison_stated is false and model_src is the EPAR. Scored same, not neg: nothing in the model fell below a bar. The model's first-use year is not public.
